observations: Files I actually read: docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, docs/PROMPTS.md, the request JSON (script for page 01 and boundary page 02, recorded first reading), source/original.txt, source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md. I opened these images with Read and looked at them: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-01.png, workflow/storyboards/page-01.png and workflow/review/page-01.png. I read workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-01.svg in full and grepped the numbered page-01.svg for its text. None of these files was unreadable. I did not open the reading-flow overlay SVG or the character-sheet PNGs.

The PNGs match the current SVGs. The unnumbered SVG has the caption box at (48,48,286x106) with 'A busy day at / Dr. Ananya's clinic.'. Meera's balloons are at (44,672) and (304,768) with the same line breaks, and Ananya's balloon is at (626,672). The tails end at (297,941), (393,939) and (852,961), which is exactly what the PNG shows. The numbered PNG differs only by the grey beat footers ('1 / A warm, busy morning at the clinic', etc.), and those match the numbered SVG text.

The script matches the source, page 1 panels 1-3. The caption and Ananya's line are verbatim. The source's single Meera line is split at the ellipsis into two balloons, 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' and 'I wish everything were easier to manage!', in the same order and with the same speaker. Nothing is removed, and no other speaker's line falls between them.

Motive chain: Meera's wish in 01-2 is the stated problem. Ananya's 'Let's make the rest simpler' in 01-3 directly answers it, and she is shown looking at the desk. That answer motivates the onboarding on page 2, and the page expectation ('How will Dr. Ananya make the busy work simpler?') is set up.

Unnumbered scan: the caption sits at the top left of the wide top tier. In the lower-left tall panel, Meera's two balloons step down from top left (y 672) to middle right (y 768), so they read as one continuous complaint. Ananya's single balloon then sits at the top of the right panel. The layout gives one obvious left-to-right, top-to-bottom path, and no balloon pair could be mistaken for a reply from another speaker.

First-reader concern: the first tail stops just short of the meera placeholder box. In the composed preview (workflow/review/page-01.png) the tail tip at (297,941) lands on the top-left of Meera's hair. Her open mouth and phone-at-ear pose make both balloons clearly hers. This exists only in the placeholder and is resolved in the art.

First-reader concern: the spatial relation between the two characters is first set up in 01-3. In the preview, 01-2 is a frontal desk shot from the queue side. 01-3 shows Ananya at the right with her hand at her chin, looking left toward the same desk, where Meera is still on the phone writing in the register in the background. Her gaze leads the eye back to the problem, then her balloon resolves it. This is acceptable and intended (script 01-3 scene and production.before).
01-1 is silent for Ananya. The preview shows her welcoming a patient in at the doorway with an open left hand, which carries the establishing beat without dialogue.

transitions.observation: From the exterior welcome to the inside reception desk on the same morning. The preview's 01-1 shows the reception desk with a phone and registers through the glass door, and 01-2 cuts to that desk with Meera on the phone. No caption is needed because the place is visibly continuous.

Meera's wish ends 01-2. 01-3 shows Ananya watching the same desk, with Meera still on the call in the background, and her line answers the wish. The cause and the reaction are adjacent on the same tier.

Ananya's resolve leads into page 2's caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.'. The page 02 SVG and preview show an evening window and a laptop over Ananya's shoulder, so the time and place change is marked by the caption and the evening light (02-1 transition.bridge). The decision is followed directly by the action.

readingReview.comparison: My comparison agrees with the recorded first reading: caption, Meera's two balloons, then Ananya's reply, which is the intended dialogue order [1],[1,2],[1]. The first reader saw no skipped reply, and I agree. Ananya's line answers Meera's wish. The two concerns it raised exist only in the placeholders: the weak first tail and the fact that the characters' relative positions are only set up in 01-3. I checked both against the composed preview and the art (the tail reaches Meera's head, and 01-3 places Meera behind Ananya's gaze). Neither needs a change, and nothing is left unresolved.
